title: Contemporary Doenjang-Gochujang Lamb Shoulder
shortDescription: Boneless lamb-shoulder steaks are marinated with doenjang, gochujang, pear, and sesame, grilled to 145°F / 63°C, and rested three minutes.
culturalContext: This contemporary recipe applies Korean fermented-paste seasoning to lamb shoulder, a combination without a single traditional standard. The descriptive Korean name and flavor balance require cultural and language review.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Outdoor grill or approved electric grill

ingredients.preparation: six steaks about 2 cm / 3/4 inch thick; do not wash

mixOrder: Whisk doenjang, gochujang, pear, rice syrup, and water.
marinadeOrSeasoning.marinationVessel: Nonreactive covered container at or below 40°F / 4°C
marinadeOrSeasoning.maximumPracticalMarinationWarning: Do not exceed 12 hours without test-cook approval; salty fermented pastes can dominate.
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: Reserve any serving sauce before the marinade contacts raw lamb.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard marinade after raw-lamb contact; do not brush it on cooked meat.
substitutions: Use verified gluten-free doenjang, gochujang, and tamari only after label review.

instructions.heading: Portion without washing
instructions.action: Keep lamb cold and portion into even shoulder steaks if not already cut; do not wash raw meat.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Steaks are about 2 cm / 3/4 inch thick.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a dedicated raw-meat board and wash hands after handling.

instructions.heading: Mix marinade
instructions.action: Whisk all marinade ingredients; reserve any serving sauce before raw contact.
instructions.safetyNote: Verify doenjang and gochujang allergen labels.

instructions.heading: Marinate cold
instructions.action: Coat lamb, cover, and refrigerate 4 hours.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Steaks remain cold and evenly coated.
instructions.safetyNote: Never marinate meat at room temperature.

instructions.heading: Preheat two zones
instructions.action: Preheat medium-high and cooler grill zones; remove lamb and discard raw-contact marinade.
instructions.safetyNote: Sugar and pastes can burn; keep a cooler zone available.

instructions.heading: Grill and measure
instructions.action: Grill, turning as needed, until each steak reaches at least 145°F / 63°C in its thickest point.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Surface is browned and every steak reaches at least 145°F / 63°C.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a calibrated thermometer; color is not a safety test.

instructions.heading: Rest three minutes
instructions.action: Move with clean tongs to a clean platter and rest at least 3 minutes before slicing.
instructions.safetyNote: The three-minute rest is part of the minimum whole-cut lamb safety endpoint.

grillSetup: Use medium-high direct and cooler zones; clean the grates, control paste scorching, and segregate raw and cooked tools.
targetInternalTemperature: At least 145°F / 63°C in the thickest part of every whole-cut lamb steak, followed by a 3-minute rest.
visualDonenessCues: Fermented-paste coating is browned but not charred
Every steak reaches 145°F / 63°C and rests 3 minutes
foodSafetyNotes: Cook whole-cut lamb steaks to at least 145°F / 63°C and rest at least 3 minutes.
Do not wash raw lamb; segregate hands, boards, utensils, marinade, and serviceware.
Control flare-ups and sugar scorching with a cooler grill zone.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Verify every packaged-ingredient label and segregate tools for diners with allergies.

substitutions: Do not substitute ground lamb; ground lamb requires 160°F / 71°C.
Verify all fermented-paste labels before any gluten-free claim.
ingredientSourcing: Ask for boneless lamb-shoulder steaks of even thickness.
Refrigerate lamb promptly and use intact, in-date packages.
makeAhead: Mix marinade 1 day ahead; marinate only within the refrigerated range.
storage: Refrigerate cooked lamb within 2 hours in shallow covered containers and use within 3 to 4 days.
leftovers: Slice only what will be served and refrigerate the remainder promptly.
servingSuggestions: Slice across the grain after the rest.
Serve with crisp vegetables and individual dipping sauce portions.

faq.question: Can I use ground lamb?
faq.answer: Not with this endpoint. Ground lamb requires 160°F / 71°C and a separate method.

faq.question: Why rest three minutes?
faq.answer: The rest is part of the safe minimum endpoint for whole-cut lamb.

metaDescription: Grill Korean-inspired fermented-paste lamb-shoulder steaks with cold marination, two heat zones, a 145°F endpoint, and a three-minute rest.
sourcesAndEditorialNotes: Editorial framing: contemporary adaptation; no canonical-tradition claim.
